summary: Stanford dropout Elizabeth Holmes founded Theranos in 2003 and raised billions selling a finger-prick blood-testing machine that never worked, putting patients at risk with faulty results until the company collapsed in 2018.

evidence.note: Holmes's birth in Washington DC and wealthy family background
Singapore internship, patent filing and founding of Real-Time Cures after dropping out
Safeway and Walgreens deals and lab-developed-test regulatory loophole
chief scientist Ian Gibbons's suicide attempt and death in 2013
glowing 2014 Fortune cover story and press credulity
CMS inspection finds dangerously inaccurate patient test results
Carreyrou's 2015 WSJ exposé and the Cramer interview counterattack
Theranos dissolved in 2018; charges against Holmes and Balwani pending
Holmes's life at release time: San Francisco, dating, ongoing cases

notes: Main span ends at the 2018 dissolution and indictment; her 2022 conviction postdates the episode. Balwani is secondary as Theranos president and enforcer. Brief China and Singapore periods in her youth left out of setting as passing segments.
